summary: Chinese has no future tense. A time word is often enough: 我明天去北京 ‘I’m going to Beijing tomorrow’. Before the verb, a few words add the kind of future: 要 — it is decided or near (我下星期要出国; 快要 / 就要 … 了 ‘about to’); 会 — a prediction, ‘will (probably)’ (明天会很冷); 打算 / 计划 — an intention, a plan (我打算明年出国); 想 — a wish, ‘would like to’ (S07). The verb itself never changes. The negative is 不: 不会 ‘won’t’, 不打算 ‘don’t intend to’, 不去 ‘won’t go’; 不要 is ‘don’t!’ or ‘I don’t want to’, not a neutral ‘won’t’. Time words for the future — 明天, 下星期 / 下周, 下个月, 明年, 以后 — stand before the verb, and a plan takes no 了.

head: Word
Says
Example
rows: 我明天去北京。 I’m going to Beijing tomorrow.
我下星期要出国。 I’m going abroad next week.
明天会很冷。 It will be cold tomorrow.
我们打算在国外待两个星期。 We plan to stay abroad for two weeks.
我想去国外旅行。 I’d like to travel abroad.
blocks.caption: No future tense — a time word, plus 要, 会, 打算

items.title: 要 — decided, near
points: 我明年要出国。 I’m going abroad next year (it’s settled).
火车快要开了！ The train is about to leave!

items.title: 会 — predicted
points: 明天会很冷。 It will be cold tomorrow.
你会喜欢北京的。 You’ll like Beijing.

items.title: 打算 — intended
points: 我打算明年出国。 I intend to go abroad next year.
你暑假打算去哪里？ Where are you planning to go in the summer?

blocks.title: The time word does most of the work
blocks.text: As with the past, the verb does not change: 我明天去, 我昨天去了, 我每天去. When the time is clear, nothing else is needed; 要, 会 and 打算 add how sure or how planned it is.

blocks.title: Saying ‘won’t’
blocks.text: 不会 ‘won’t (I don’t expect it)’: 他不会来. 不打算 ‘don’t intend to’. 不去 ‘won’t go (I’ve decided)’. But 不要 + verb is a command to someone (不要走！ ‘don’t go!’) or a strong ‘I don’t want to’ — not a neutral ‘won’t’.

blocks.title: 会 has two jobs
blocks.text: 会 + verb is ‘will (probably)’ here; it is also ‘can, know how to’ (会说中文, C05). 他不会来 ‘he won’t come’ but 他不会开车 ‘he can’t drive’ — the verb and the situation decide.

blocks.title: About to happen
blocks.text: 快要 … 了 / 快 … 了 and 就要 … 了 mean ‘be about to’: 我们快要到了 ‘we’re nearly there’, 明天就要放假了 ‘the holidays start tomorrow’. With a time word use 就要, not 快要: *明天快要放假了.

head: Time word
Meaning
rows: 下星期 / 下周 / 下个星期
blocks.caption: Time words for the future — before the verb; next year is 明年, not *下年

blocks.title: No 了 for plans
blocks.text: A plan has not happened: 我明天要预订酒店 (no 了). In the future, 了 only marks one step done before the next: 明天我预订了酒店就给你打电话 ‘tomorrow, once I’ve booked the hotel, I’ll call you’.

blocks.title: Asking about plans
blocks.text: 你明年打算做什么？ · 你什么时候出国？ · 你会来吗？ · 你下个星期要去哪里？ — the question word stands where the answer goes (S10).

askYourself: Is the time already clear from a time word? → the plain verb may be enough (我明天去).
Is it decided, or about to happen? → 要 (快要 / 就要 … 了).
Is it a prediction or a guess? → 会.
Is it an intention or a plan? → 打算 / 计划.
Is it only a wish? → 想.
Negative? → 不会 / 不打算 / 不 + verb — 不要 is a command.
Is there a time word with ‘about to’? → 就要 … 了, not 快要.
steps: Put the time word before the verb.
Add the kind of future: 要, 会, 打算.
Negate with 不 (不会, 不打算).

traps: *我去北京明天 → 我明天去北京 (time before the verb).
*明天快要放假了 → 明天就要放假了.
*我明天要预订了酒店 → 我明天要预订酒店 (no 了 for a plan).
他不会来 (won’t come) ≠ 他不会开车 (can’t drive).
*我打算到出国 → 我打算出国 (no word for ‘to’).
下星期, 下个月 — but 明年, not *下年.

quiz.why: 会 predicts: ‘will (probably)’; the time word comes first.

quiz.q: ‘I intend to go abroad next year.’
quiz.why: The time word stands before the verb, and 打算 needs no word for ‘to’.
With a time word, 就要 … 了; 快要 takes no time word.
不会 = won’t (a prediction); 不要来 is ‘don’t come!’ or ‘doesn’t want to come’.
Next year is 明年; next week and next month take 下 (下星期, 下个月).

quiz.q: ‘Where are you planning to go in the summer holidays?’
quiz.why: The question word stays in place, no 吗 after it, and the time word comes first.

notes.text: Greek θα + verb (θα πάω ‘I’ll go’) is a particle before the verb, like 会 / 要; but Greek also changes the verb (θα πηγαίνω ‘I’ll be going’) — Chinese never does.
Russian uses the perfective present as its future (поеду ‘I’ll go’) or буду + infinitive (буду читать); Chinese uses time words and 会 / 要 before an unchanged verb.
Iré (future tense) ~ 我会去; voy a ir ‘I’m going to go’ ~ 我要去 / 我打算去. Like Spanish mañana voy, Chinese often uses the plain verb with a time word: 我明天去.
‘Will’ ~ 会 (a prediction), ‘be going to’ ~ 要 / 打算, ‘I’m leaving tomorrow’ ~ 我明天走 with no extra word. ‘Won’t’ is 不会, not 不要.
Futur simple (j’irai) ~ 我会去; futur proche (je vais partir) ~ 我要走; demain je pars ~ 我明天走.
German usually says the future with the present and a time word — morgen fahre ich nach Berlin — exactly like 我明天去北京; werden + infinitive (es wird kalt sein) is close to 会 (明天会很冷).
Hindi has a future form with endings for person and gender (जाऊँगा / जाऊँगी ‘I’ll go’); Chinese adds 会 / 要 to a verb that never changes.
Persian xāham raft ‘I will go’ uses xāstan ‘to want’, as Chinese uses 要 ‘want’ for a decided future; in speech both prefer the present + a time word (fardā miravam ~ 我明天去).
Arabic marks the future with سَ / سَوْفَ before the conjugated imperfect (سَأُسَافِرُ ‘I will travel’); Chinese has no conjugation: 我会去, 我要去.
Hebrew has a future conjugation with prefixes and suffixes (אֶסַּע ‘I will travel’, נִסַּע ‘we will travel’); Chinese uses one bare verb with 要, 会 or a time word.
Turkish -ecek / -acak is a future suffix with person endings (gideceğim ‘I will go’); Chinese 我会去 / 我要去 uses separate words.
Japanese has no future tense either: 明日行きます is ‘I go / I’ll go tomorrow’, like 我明天去; つもり ‘intention’ ~ 打算.
Korean -ㄹ 거예요 (갈 거예요 ‘I’ll go’) is a future-like ending; Chinese puts 会 / 要 before the verb instead.
Finnish has no future tense: menen huomenna ‘I go tomorrow’ ~ 我明天去.
Hungarian mostly uses the present for the future (holnap megyek ‘I’ll go tomorrow’), like 我明天去; fog + infinitive (menni fogok) is close to 会 / 要.
Swahili -ta- is a future prefix in the verb (nitaenda ‘I will go’); Chinese puts 会 or 要 before a bare verb.
Vietnamese sẽ ~ 会 / 要 (tôi sẽ đi ‘I will go’), sắp ~ 快要 (sắp đi ‘about to go’), and often just a time word (mai tôi đi ~ 我明天去).
Polysynthetic languages usually mark the future with a suffix inside the verb word; Chinese adds 会 or 要 as separate words before an unchanged verb.

seeAlso.note: werden + infinitive (ich werde fahren) exists, but German mostly uses the present with a time word (morgen fahre ich) — just like 我明天去.
Arabic سَ- / سَوْفَ + the imperfect (سَأُسَافِرُ ‘I will travel’); Chinese 我会去 / 我要去 with an unchanged verb.
Hebrew has a future conjugation (אֶסַּע ‘I will travel’); Chinese marks the future with time words and 要 / 会 / 打算.
The time words before the verb (S14) are the main way to place an action in the future.
